newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai phone companies unable to cut call charges.
newsitem.headline: Thai phone companies unable to cut call charges.

text.p: Fixed-line phone operators Thai Telephone and Telecommunication Plc and TelecomAsia Plc said on Tuesday they are unable to reduce long distance call charges because of current financial restraints.
The state's Telephone Organisation of Thailand recently recommended that the companies reduce charges for long distance calls.

"Having talked with the Telephone Organisation of Thailand (TOT) on May 12, 1997, Thai Telephone and Telecommunication Plc concluded the charges for long distance calls could not be reduced," the company said in a statement issued on Tuesday.
Thai Telephone, which started operations four years ago and has recently installed 1.5 million provincial fixed-lines, said its ability to repay debtors would have been harmed by a charge reduction.

"If the company abides by the TOT's recommendation (to reduce the charge fee) its business may be aggravated and default may happen as those creditors believe it could not conform to statements in loan contracts," the statement said.
TelecomAsia, which last year completed a 2.6 million fixed-line expansion programme in Bangkok, cited similar financial and loan contract constraints behind its decision to maintain current charges.
Both companies said they were willing to reconsider the TOT's proposals to cut charges once consultant Coopers and Lybrand finished a study into the issue.
